src: Hi, this is Elena and I'm going to be presenting our work, Detecting Unassimilated Borrowings in Spanish: An Annotated Corpus and Approaches to Modeling.
ref: 大家好，我是Elena，我将向大家介绍我们的工作——检测西班牙语中的未同化借词：注释语料库和建模方法。
tgt: 在今天，我是埃琳娜。 我将介绍我们关于检测西班牙语中无关联借用词的工作，以及标注语料库和建模方法。

src: So we're going to be covering what lexical borrowing is, the task that we proposed, the dataset that we have released and some models that we explored.
ref: 我们将讨论什么是词汇借用、我们提出的任务、我们已经发布的数据集，以及我们探索的一些模型。
tgt: 因此，我们将涵盖词源借用的定义、我们提出的方法任务、发布的数据集，以及我们探索的一些模型。

src: But to begin with, what is lexical borrowing and why it matters as an NLP task?
ref: 首先，什么是词汇借用，为什么它作为一个自然语言处理任务很重要？
tgt: 首先，什么是词源借用？

src: Well, lexical borrowing is basically the incorporation of words from one language into another language.
ref: 总的来说，词汇借用是将一种语言的单词并入另一种语言中。
tgt: 它为何重要？ 嗯，词源借用基本上是指将一种语言中的词语引入另一种语言。

src: For instance, in Spanish we use words that come from English.
ref: 例如，在西班牙语中，我们会使用来自英语的单词。
tgt: 例如，在西班牙语中，我们使用了许多来自英语的词汇。

src: And here you have a few examples, words such as podcast, app, and online crowdfunding, all these are English words that we sometimes use in Spanish.
ref: 这里有几个例子，比如podcast、app和online crowdfunding等单词，所有这些都是我们有时会在西班牙语中使用的英语单词。
tgt: 这里有几个例子，比如播客、应用程序、在线、众筹这些词都是英语词汇，我们有时会在西班牙语中使用。

src: Lexical borrowing is a type of linguistic borrowing um which is basically reproducing in one language patterns of other languages.
ref: 词汇借用是一种语言学借用，本质上是在一种语言中再现其他语言的模式。
tgt: 词源借用是一种语言借用，是一种本质上是在一种语言中重复使用另一种语言的模式。

src: And borrowing and code switching have sometimes been compared and described as a continuum, code switching being ah the thing that bilinguals do where they mix two languages at the same time.
ref: 借用和语码转换有时会被比较并被描述为一个连续体，语码转换就是双语者同时混合两种语言时所做的事情。
tgt: 借用和代码切换有时被相提并论，并被描述为一种连续体。 代码切换是指双语者将两种语言混合使用的行为。

src: There are however some differences between lexical borrowing and code-switching.
ref: 然而，词汇借用和语码转换之间存在一些差异。
tgt: 然而，词源借用和代码切换之间存在一些区别。

src: We're going to be focusing on lexical borrowing.
ref: 我们将重点讨论词汇借用。
tgt: 我们将重点讨论词源借用。

src: Code switching is something that is done by bilinguals and by definition the code switches are not integrated into any of the languages in use, whereas lexical borrowing is something that is also done by monolinguals.
ref: 语码转换是由双语者完成的，根据定义，语码转换并没有融入到任何一种正在使用的语言中，而词汇借用也可以由单语者完成。
tgt: 代码切换是双语者所做的事情，而根据定义，代码切换者并非任何一种语言的使用者，而词源借用也是单语者会做的事情。

src: The borrowings will comply with the grammar of the recipient language. And borrowings can eventually be integrated into the recipient language. So why is borrowing an interesting phenomenon? Well, from the point of view of linguistics, borrowing is a manifestation of of how languages change and how they interact. And also lexical borrowings are a source of new words.
ref: 借词要符合接受者语言的语法。 借词最终可以融入到接受者的语言中。 那么，为什么说借词是一种有趣的现象呢？ 从语言学的角度来看，借词是语言如何变化以及它们如何相互作用的一种表现。 而且词汇借用也是新词的来源之一。
tgt: 借用的词汇将符合接收语言的语法，而这些借用词汇最终可能被融入接收语言中。

src: Here you have some examples of lexical borrowings that have been incorporated into the Spanish language as new words.
ref: 这里有一些词汇借用的例子，这些借词已经作为新词融入到西班牙语语言中。
tgt: 尝试。

src: In terms of NLP ah borrowings are a common source of out-of-vocabulary words. And in fact, automatically detecting lexical borrowings ah has proven to be useful for NLP downstream tasks such as parsing, text-to-speech synthesis or machine translation.
ref: 就自然语言处理而言，借词是词汇单词之外的一个常见来源。 而事实上，自动地检测词汇借用已被证明对自然语言处理下游任务有用，例如解析、文本-语音合成或机器翻译。
tgt: 事实上，自动检测词源借用对于自然语言处理的下游任务非常有用，例如分析文本、分词或机器翻译。

src: There has been a growing interest in the influence of English on other languages ah particularly ah related to English lexical borrowings, borrowings which sometimes have been called Anglicisms.
ref: 人们越来越关注英语对其他语言的影响，尤其是与英语词汇借用有关的影响，这些借词有时被称为英语的借词。
tgt: 近年来，人们对英语对其他语言的影响日益关注，特别是英语的词源借用。 这些借用有时被称为英语化词。

src: And here, you have some examples of ah work on automatic detection of borrowings in ah some of these languages.
ref: 在这里，我们举了一些关于这些语言中借词的自动检测工作的例子。
tgt: 这里有一些在某些语言中自动检测借用词的研究事例。

src: So the task that we propose is to detect unassimilated lexical borrowings in Spanish newswire.
ref: 因此，我们提出的任务是检测西班牙语新闻专线中未同化的词汇借用。
tgt: 因此，我们提出提出。

src: Which means that we are interested in extracting ah words borrowed from other languages that are being used in Spanish newspapers but that have not been integrated or assimilated into the recipient language.
ref: 也就是说，我们感兴趣的是提取从其他语言中借用的单词，这些单词正在西班牙语报纸中使用，但尚未融入或同化到接收者的语言中。
tgt: 因此，我们你提出可以称为的是提取从其他语言借用的词汇。 这些词汇正在被西班牙语报纸使用，但尚未被吸收或融入目标语言中。

src: So not yet integrated into Spanish.
ref: 所以还没有融入西班牙语。
tgt: 这些词尚未融入西班牙语中。

src: Here you have an example.
ref: 让我来举个例子。
tgt: 这里有一个例子。

src: This is a sentence in Spanish: Las prendas bestsellers se estampan con motivos florales, animal print o retales tipo patchwork.
ref: 这是一个西班牙语的句子：Las Prendas Bestsellers Se estampan con motivos florales，Animal print o retales tipo patchwork.
tgt: 这是一句西班牙语报纸使用畅销服饰带有花卉图案、动物印花或拼布风格的条纹。

src: Um, and as you can see, there are three spans of texts which are actually English words like bestseller, animal print and patchwork.
ref: 嗯，正如大家所看到的，有三个跨度的文本实际上是英语单词，比如bestseller、animal print和patchwork。
tgt: 如您所见，有三处文字是实际的英语单词，比如 bestsellers。

src: These are the type of spans that we are interested in extracting and detecting.
ref: 这些是我们所感兴趣的提取和检测的跨度类型。
tgt: 这些是我们所关注的span类型。

src: There has been previous word on Anglicism detection ah which consists consisted of a CRF model for Anglicism detection on Spanish Newswire. This model achieved an F1 score of eighty six.
ref: 之前已经有关于英语检测的单词，由西班牙语新闻专线上用于英语检测的CRF模型组成。 这个模型取得了86分的F1分数。
tgt: 关于英语词检测的研究，这些研究采用了一种CRF模型来检测西班牙语新闻电报中的英语词。

src: But there were some limitations both um in the dataset and the modeling approach.
ref: 但是在数据集和建模方法方面都有一些局限性。
tgt: 该模型单模型早期说存在一些局限，包括数据集和建模方法方面。

src: So the dataset focused exclusively on one source of news, consisted only of headlines.
ref: 该数据集只关注新闻的一个来源，并且仅包含头条新闻。
tgt: 因此，数据集仅专注于单一新闻来源，且仅包含标题。

src: And also there was an overlap in the borrowings that appear in the training set and the test set. This prevented the assessment of whether the modeling approach could actually generalize to previously unseen borrowings. So what we aim is to tackle some of these limitations in the task. So to begin we, to begin with, we created a new dataset. Ah the aim at a new dataset that was annotated with lexical borrowings and the aim was to create a test set that was as difficult as possible. So there would be minimal overlap in words and topics between the training set and test set. And as a result, well, the test set comes from sources and dates that we're not seeing in the training set.
ref: 此外，在训练集和测试集中出现的借词也有重叠。 这使我们无法评估建模方法是否可以实际概括到以前未见过的借词。 因此，我们的目标是解决任务中的一些局限性。 为此，首先我们创建了一个新的数据集。 我们的目标是创建一个新的数据集，该数据集使用词汇借词进行注释，目的是创建一个尽可能困难的测试集。 因此，训练集和测试集之间的单词和主题的重叠程度会很小。 因此，测试集来自我们在训练集中看不到的来源和日期。
tgt: 此外，借用词在训练集和测试集之间存在重叠，因此无法评估建模方法几个借用进行标注与训练集完全不同，在时间上也没有重叠。

src: Here you can see that there's no overlap in the in the time. It's also, the test set is also very borrowing-dense.
ref: 在这里大家可以看到，在时间上没有重叠。 而且，测试集的借词密度也很高。
tgt: 此外，测试集的词汇借用现象非常密集。

src: Just to give you some numbers, if the training set contains six borrowings per each thousand tokens, the test set contained twenty borrowings per each thousand tokens.
ref: 给大家看一些数字：如果训练集每1000个令牌包含6六个借词，那么测试集每1000个令牌包含20个借词。
tgt: 这里给出一些数据：如果训练集每千个词包含六个借用词，那么测试集则每千个词包含二十个借用词。

src: The test set contained as many out of vocabulary words as possible.
ref: 测试集包含了尽可能多的词汇表外的单词。
tgt: 测试集包含大量词汇表外词。

src: In fact, ninety two percent of the borrowings in the test set are OOV. So, they were not seen during training.
ref: 事实上，测试集中92%的借词都是OOV。 因此，在训练期间看不到它们。
tgt: 事实上，测试集中的借用词有百分之九十二都是未登录词，即在训练过程中未曾出现过。

src: And the corpus consisted basically of a collection of texts that came from different sources of Spanish newspapers. And ah it was annotated by hand ah using two tags.
ref: 而语料库总的来说是由来自不同来源的西班牙报纸的文本集合而成的。 而且它是用两个标签手工注释的。
tgt: 基本上由来自不同来源的西班牙语报纸文本组成。

src: One for English lexical borrowings which is the majority of lexical borrowings in Spanish, and then the label other for borrowings from other languages.
ref: 一个标签用于注释英语词汇借词，这是西班牙语中的大多数词汇借词，然后另一个标签用于注释来自其他语言的借词。
tgt: 它是一个是英语词汇借用词，西班牙语中词汇借用的主流类型。 另一个标签是其他，用于标注来自其他语言的借用词。

src: We use CONLL formats and we used BIO encoding so that we could encode ah single token borrowings such as app or multi token borrowings such as machine learning.
ref: 我们使用CONLL格式和BIO编码，这样我们就可以编码单个令牌借词，比如app，或多个令牌借词，比如machine learning。
tgt: 我们使用纽扣NLL格式，并采用了BIO编码，这样我们就可以编码单个词素的借用词，比如app，以及多个词素的借用词，比如machine learning。

src: These are the numbers of the corpus. As you can see, it amounts to roughly three hundred seventy thousand tokens.
ref: 这些是语料库的数字。 如大家所见，这相当于大约有37万个令牌。
tgt: 这些是语料库的规模，如你所见，大约有三十七万个词素。

src: And here you have the number of spans that were labeled as English and the spans that were labeled as other borrowings and how many of them were unique. And here you have a couple of examples of the of the set of the dataset. As you can see for instance here, we have ah in the first example, we have the borrowing batch cooking which is a multi word borrowing. And we have annotated it using the BIO um encode. So the BIO was used for words in Spanish so not for words that were not borrowed.
ref: 这包含了被标记为英语的跨度数量和标记为其他借词的跨度数量，以及它们中有多少是独一无二的。 这里有几个关于数据集集合的例子。 正如大家所看到的，例如，在第一个例子中，我们有一个借词的批处理，这是一个多单词借词。 而且我们已经使用BIO编码对其进行了注释。 因此，BIO用于西班牙语中的单词，而不是用于未借用的单词。
tgt: 这里你看到的是被标记为英语的词素片段数量，以及被标记为其他借用词的词素片段数量，以及其中有多少是唯一的。

src: And here in this second example, you have benching and crash which are also labeled as borrowings from English. So, once we had the dataset, we explored several models for the task of extracting and detecting these lexical borrowings. The first one that we tried was the conditional random field model. Ah, this was the model that had been used on previous work. And we used the same handcrafted features from that from those from that work.
ref: 在这个第二个例子中，大家可以看到benching和crash这两个词也被标记为是从英语借来的。 因此，一旦我们拥有了数据集，我们就为提取和检测这些词汇借词的任务探索了几个模型。 我们首先尝试的是条件随机场模型。 这是在之前工作中使用过的模型。 我们使用了与那次工作中相同的手工制作的特征。
tgt: 这里你可以看到一些数据集的示例，例如这里我们看到第一个例子中，我们有借用词batch cooking，这是一个多也就是之前研究中使用过的模型，我们使用了相同的手工设计的特征。

src: As you can see, these are the features. These are binary features such as the word or the token in upper case? Is it title titlecase? Is it a quotation mark?
ref: 如大家所见，这些都是特征。 这些都是二进制特征，例如大写的单词或令牌？ 是标题标签吗？ 是引号吗？
tgt: 如你所见，这些是二元特征，例如单词或词元是否为大写，是否为驼峰命名法，是否为引号等。

src: Things like that, which are the type of features that one would expect in a named entity recognition task.
ref: 诸如此类的东西，这是人们在命名实体识别任务中所期望的特征类型。
tgt: 这些特征正是命名实体识别任务中预期会用到的类型。

src: These are the results that we got.
ref: 这就是我们得到的结果。
tgt: 这些是我们得到的结果。

src: We obtain fifty five F1 score using the the CRF model with handcrafted features.
ref: 我们使用具有手工制作特征的CRF模型获得55分的F1分数。
tgt: 我们手工设计特征的CRF模型获得了55的F1分数，这与之前相比有巨大差异。

src: Which is a huge different difference um compared to the reported F1 score of eighty six, which was the result obtained with the same CRF model, same features but on a different dataset also for Spanish lexical borrowing detection.
ref: 与报告的86分F1分数相比，这是一个巨大的差异，F1分数是用相同的CRF模型，相同的特征，但是在不同的数据集上获得的结果，也用于西班牙语词汇借用检测。
tgt: 而之前报告的F1分数为86，那是使用相同CRF模型和相同特征，但在不同数据集上得到的结果。

src: So, this proves that the dataset that we created is more difficult and that we needed to explore more sophisticated models for these tasks.
ref: 因此，这证明了我们创建的数据集更加困难，我们需要探索更复杂的模型用于这些任务。
tgt: 因此，这些结果证明我们创建的数据集是更具挑战性的，需要更复杂的模型来应对这项任务。

src: So, we tested two transformer based models.
ref: 因此，我们测试了两个基于转换器的模型。
tgt: 测试了两种基于Transformer的模型。

src: We used BETO which is a monolingual BERT model trained for Spanish and also multilingual BERT.
ref: 我们使用了BETO，这是一个单语BERT模型，针对西班牙语和多语言BERT训练的模型。
tgt: 我们使用了BERT，这是一种专为西班牙语训练的单语BERT模型以及多语种BERT。

src: Both models we use them through the transformers library by HuggingFace.
ref: 我们通过HuggingFace的转换器库使用这两个模型。
tgt: 这两种模型我们都通过Transformer库使用Hugging Face进行。

src: These are the results that we got.
ref: 这就是我们得到的结果。
tgt: 这是我们得到的结果。

src: As you can see, multilingual BERT performs better than BETO both on the development set and on the test set and across all metrics.
ref: 正如大家所看到的，多语言BERT在开发集和测试集以及所有指标上的表现都优于BETO。
tgt: 正如你所见，多语种BERT的表现优于BERT，在开发集和测试集上以及所有指标上均如此。

src: Just so we have ah an idea to compare, the CRF model obtained an eighty two.
ref: 正因为如此，我们有了一个比较的想法，CRF模型获得了82分。
tgt: 啊，这让我们有了一个当可以比较的基准。

src: The CRF model obtained a fifty five obtained a fifty five F1 score, whereas the multilingual BERT obtained eighty two, which is a big difference. So, once that we had those results, we asked ourselves another question which is, could we find a BiLSTM-CRF model, feed it with different types of embeddings, embeddings that encode different types of linguistic information and perform outperform the results obtained by transformer based models? So in order to do so, we ran some preliminary experiments, we we run this by BiLSTM-CRF model using flare library. And we tried experimented with different type of embeddings like transformer-based but also fast-text, character embeddings, and so on.
ref: CRF模型获得了55分，获得了55分的F1分数，而多语言BERT获得了82分，这是一个很大的差异。 所以，一旦我们得到了这些结果，我们就会问自己另一个问题，那就是，我们能否找到一个BiLSTM-CRF模型，为它提供不同类型的嵌入，嵌入对不同类型的语言信息进行编码，并执行优于基于转换器的模型获得的结果？ 因此，为了做到这一点，我们进行了一些初步实验，我们使用flare库通过BiLSTM-CRF模型运行这些实验。 我们尝试了不同类型的嵌入，比如基于转换器但也是快速的文本、字符嵌入等等。
tgt: CRF模型获得了82分，CRF模型在F1分数上得分为55，而Flair库运行了这个BiLSTM-CRF模型，并尝试了不同类型的嵌入向量，例如基于Transformer的嵌入以及FastText，还有字符级嵌入等。

src: What we found out was that transformer-based embeddings performed better than non contextualized embeddings, that the combination of English BERT and Spanish BETO embeddings outperform multilingual BERT embeddings.
ref: 我们发现，基于转换器的嵌入比非情境化的嵌入表现得更好，英语BERT和西班牙语BETO嵌入的组合比多语言BERT嵌入表现得更好。
tgt: 我们发现基于Transformer的嵌入向量优于非上下文相关的嵌入向量。 英文BERT和西班牙语BERTO的嵌入组合在多语言BERT嵌入中表现更优。

src: And that BPE embeddings produced better F1 and character embeddings produce better recall.
ref: BPE嵌入产生了更好的F1，字符嵌入产生了更好的调用。
tgt: BPE嵌入对F1分数更高，而字符级嵌入对召回率更高。

src: With that in mind, these were the best performing results that we got.
ref: 考虑到这一点，这些是我们获得的表现最好的结果。
tgt: 基于此，这些是我们获得的最佳性能结果。

src: Both models were BiLSTM-CRF models using flare. One was fed with BETO and BERT embeddings and BPE, and the other one BETO and BERT embeddings and BPE and also character embeddings.
ref: 两个模型均为使用flare的BiLSTM-CRF模型。 一个是BETO和BERT 嵌入和BPE，另一个是BETO和BERT嵌入和BPE，还有字符嵌入。
tgt: 这两个模型都是BiLSTM-CRF模型，使用了CLL，一个使用了BERTO和BERT嵌入以及BPE，另一个则使用了BERTO、BERT和BERT嵌入，此外还使用了字符级嵌入。

src: We all know that recent natural language processing advances have been made possible by the use of pretrained language models such as BERT.

src: However, there are still a number of limitations.

src: Due to the complex morphology that is expressed by most morphologically rich languages, the ubiquitous byte pair encoding tokenization algorithm that I used cannot extract the exact subword lexical units, meaning the morphemes, which are needed for effective representation.
ref: 由于大多数形态学上丰富的语言所表达的形态学很复杂，我使用的普遍存在的字节对编码标记化算法无法提取有效表达所需的确切子词词汇单位，即意义语素。

src: For example, here we have three Kinyarwanda words that have several morphemes in them, but the BPE algorithms cannot extract them.
ref: 例如，这里我们有三个基尼亚卢旺达语单词，其中有几个语素，但BPE算法无法提取它们。
tgt: 例如，这里有三个卢旺达语单词，每个单词都包含多个词素，但双词编码算法无法提取这些词素。

src: This is because some morphological rules produce different surface forms that hide the exact lexical information, and BPE, which is solely based on the surface forms, does not have access to this lexical model.
ref: 这是因为某些形态化规则产生不同的表面形式，隐藏了确切的词汇信息，而完全基于表面形式的BPE无法访问此词汇模型。

src: The second challenge is that even if one had access to an oracle morphological analyzer, replacing BPE tokens with morphemes is not enough to express the morphological compositionality.
ref: 第二个挑战是，即使人们能够使用甲骨文形态化分析器，用语素替换BPE令牌也不足以表达形态学组合性。

src: A third gap in the research is that new pretrained language models are most often evaluated on high resource languages. And we need to assess their applicability on low resources and diverse languages as well.
ref: 这次研究涉及的第三个空白是，新的预训练语言模型通常是在高资源语言上进行评估的。 我们还需要评估它们在低资源和多样化语言上的适用性。

src: Therefore, we present KinyaBERT, which is a simple but effective adaptation of the BERT architecture that is meant to more effectively handle morphologically rich languages.

src: The input to the model is either a sentence or a document. For example here, we have John twarahamubonye biradutangaza, which means we were surprised to find John there.

src: Which then generates morphemes contained in each of the words.

src: After this step, we make embeddings for the spee- for the part of speech tags. Embeddings for the affixes. And embeddings for the stem.

src: We then pass these embeddings through a morphology encoder, which is a small transformer encoder that is applied to each word independently. The output of the are the vectors that are contextualized with the morphological information at each word.

src: Then we form an input to the main sentence or document encoder.

src: The final output are contextualized embeddings that can be used for downstream NLP tasks.

src: For a morphological analyzer, we use finite state two level morphology principles with custom implementation that is tailored to the Kinyarwanda language.
ref: 对于形态分析器，我们使用有限状态二级形态学原则，并根据基尼亚卢旺达语语言定制实现。

src: We effectively model the morphology of all Kinyarwanda words, including verbals, nouns, demonstrative and possessive pronouns, numerals, and others.

tgt: 我们进一步将它们名词、指示代词和所有格代词、数词以及其他词类。

src: We use an unsupervised part of speech tagging algorithm. A first order factored model is used to account for morphology probability, basically the probability that is assigned by the morphological analyzer.

src: We also take into consideration the part of speech tag precedence as well as the syntactic agreements that are present in the in the input words.

src: The part of speech tagger uses a bidi bidirectional inference which improves upon the more often used Viterbi algorithm for decoding.

src: A few remarks here for positional encoding. One, the morphology encoder does not use any positional encoding. This is because each of the morphemes occupies a known slot in the morphological model. Therefore, positional information is inherent when the morphemes are given.

src: Similar to BERT, we use a masked language model pre-training objective.

src: Essentially we have to predict both the stem and the affixes that are associated with the words.

src: For affix prediction, we face some multi label classification problem. For this, we either group together affixes into a fixed number of sets and predict the set as a class label. The other option is to predict the affix probability vector. We evaluate both of these approaches in our experiments.

src: We pre-train KinyaBERT on about two and half gigabytes of Kinyarwanda text, and compare it to three baseline models. One is a multilingual model called XLM-R, that is trained on a large text corpora that is made of multiple languages.

src: All models are configured in the base architecture, which is about between a hundred and a hundred and ten million parameters, with Kinyarwanda with KinyaBERT using the least number of parameters.
